narrative:
The bank’s decision to deny your loan was based on an assessment of your overall financial profile, and the model predicted that you have a **58% chance of being a bad credit risk**—meaning there’s a more than half likelihood that you might struggle to repay the loan as agreed. Since the bank uses a threshold of 25% to make decisions, this prediction unfortunately led to the denial.

The most significant factors influencing this decision were your **loan amount, savings, and credit history**. The first and most impactful was the **size of the loan you requested**—at over **10,600 DM**, it was nearly **four times higher** than the average approved loan. A larger loan naturally means a bigger financial burden, and the bank saw this as a higher risk, especially when combined with other factors.

Your **savings account status** also played a major role. With savings below **100 DM**, you have very little financial cushion in case of unexpected expenses, which makes it harder to manage loan payments if something goes wrong. Most approved applicants had at least some savings, often much more, giving them a safety net the bank values.

Finally, your **credit history** worked *against* the prediction—this was actually the only factor that slightly *helped* your case. Unlike many applicants with a clean record, your history includes **critical or other outstanding credits**, which signals to the bank that you may already be stretched thin financially. While this wasn’t the strongest push toward approval, it didn’t outweigh the other concerns.

To improve your chances next time, focus on **reducing the loan amount** to something more in line with what others in your situation have successfully managed. **Building savings**—even small, regular deposits—would also strengthen your application by showing you can handle financial setbacks. Finally, **paying down or consolidating existing debts** could improve your credit standing, making future applications more favorable.
